summary: The two goats of Yom Kippur should look the same and be bought together. If one of them dies, this mishnah teaches what to do.

chunks.en: The two goats of Yom Kippur:
chunks.st: The mitzva of the two Yom Kippur goats, the goat sacrificed to God and the goat sent to Azazel that are brought as a pair, is as follows, ab initio:

chunks.en: the mitzvah is that both of them should be the same in looks,
chunks.st: That they will both be identical in appearance, i.e., color,

chunks.en: and in height, and in price, and be bought together.
chunks.st: and in height, and in monetary value, and their acquisition must be as one, i.e., they must be purchased together.

chunks.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן שָׁוִין, כְּשֵׁרִין.
chunks.en: And even if they are not the same, they are kosher.
chunks.st: And even if they are not identical, nevertheless, they are valid.

chunks.he: לָקַח אֶחָד הַיּוֹם וְאֶחָד לְמָחָר, כְּשֵׁרִין.
chunks.en: If he bought one today and one tomorrow, they are kosher.
chunks.st: And similarly, if he acquired one today and one tomorrow, they are valid.

chunks.en: If one of them died,
chunks.st: If one of the goats died,

chunks.en: if it died before he drew the lots,
chunks.st: if it died before the High Priest drew the lots,

chunks.en: he takes a partner for the second one.
chunks.st: he immediately takes a counterpart for the second, since neither has yet been designated.

chunks.en: And if it died after he drew the lots,
chunks.st: And if it died after the High Priest drew the lots,

chunks.he: יָבִיא זוּג אַחֵר וְיַגְרִיל עֲלֵיהֶם בַּתְּחִלָּה,
chunks.en: he brings another pair and draws lots on them from the start,
chunks.st: he brings another pair of goats and draws lots over them from the start.

chunks.en: and he says, "If the one for Hashem died,
chunks.st: After that lottery he utters a stipulation: If the one to be sacrificed to God died,

chunks.en: this one, that the lot for Hashem
chunks.st: that goat upon which the lot for God was drawn in the second lottery

chunks.en: came up on, will stand in its place.
chunks.st: shall stand in its stead;

chunks.en: And if the one for Azazel died,
chunks.st: and if the one to be sent to Azazel died,

chunks.en: this one, that the lot for Azazel
chunks.st: that goat upon which the lot for Azazel was drawn

chunks.en: came up on, will stand in its place."
chunks.st: shall stand in its stead.

chunks.en: And the second one grazes until it gets a mum,
chunks.explain: A mum is a blemish that makes an animal unfit for a korban.
chunks.st: And the second, superfluous goat, i.e., in the case where a new pair of goats was brought, should graze until it becomes unfit,

chunks.en: and it is sold, and its money goes to a gift korban,
chunks.st: at which point it will be sold, and the money received from its sale will go toward the purchase of a public gift-offering.
chunks.stMore: Although for individual sin-offerings in similar circumstances there is no remedy and it is left to die, that is not the case here,

chunks.en: because a chatas of the community is not left to die.
chunks.st: as a communal sin-offering is not left to die.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says, it should be left to die.
chunks.st: On the other hand, Rabbi Yehuda says: In this it should be left to die.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehuda said more:
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: If the blood spilled,
chunks.st: If the blood of the goat sacrificed to God spilled before it was sprinkled,

chunks.en: the goat to be sent away is left to die.
chunks.st: the scapegoat is left to die.

chunks.en: If the goat to be sent away died,
chunks.st: Similarly, if the scapegoat dies,

chunks.en: the blood is spilled out.
chunks.explain: Then they bring two new goats and start over.
chunks.st: the blood of the goat sacrificed to God should be spilled, and two other goats are brought and lots are drawn.

summary: The Kohen Gadol leans his hands on the goat for Azazel and does viduy for all of the Jewish people. When the people hear Hashem's holy Name, they bow down and answer "Baruch shem."

chunks.en: He comes to the goat that is sent away,
chunks.st: The Yom Kippur service continues: The High Priest comes over to the scapegoat,

chunks.en: and leans his two hands on it and says viduy.
chunks.st: places both his hands upon it, and confesses.

chunks.en: And this is what he would say:
chunks.st: And he would say as follows:

chunks.en: "Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.he: עָווּ פָּשְׁעוּ חָטְאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל.
chunks.en: Your people, the house of Yisrael, have done wrong, rebelled and sinned before You.
chunks.st: Your people, the house of Israel, have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You.

chunks.en: Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.en: please forgive the sins, the rebellions and the wrongs
chunks.st: grant atonement, please, for the sins, and for the wrongs, and for the rebellions

chunks.he: שֶׁעָווּ וְשֶׁפָּשְׁעוּ וְשֶׁחָטְאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: that Your people, the house of Yisrael, did wrong, rebelled and sinned before You,
chunks.st: that they have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You, Your people, the house of Israel,

chunks.he: כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרַת משֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ לֵאמֹר (ויקרא טז),
chunks.en: as it is written in the Torah of Moshe Your servant (Vayikra 16):
chunks.st: as it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant, saying:

chunks.en: 'For on this day He will forgive you,
chunks.st: “For on this day atonement shall be made for you

chunks.he: לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי יְיָ תִּטְהָרוּ.
chunks.en: to make you clean from all your sins; before Hashem you will be clean.'"
chunks.st: to cleanse you of all your sins; before the Lord you shall be purified” (Leviticus 16:30).

chunks.en: And the Kohanim and the people standing in the azarah,
chunks.st: And the priests and the people standing in the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: when they would hear the special Name of Hashem
chunks.st: when they would hear the Explicit Name

words.note: Hashem's holy Name, said only by the Kohen Gadol in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: coming out of the mouth of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: emerging from the mouth of the High Priest, when the High Priest did not use one of the substitute names for God,

chunks.he: הָיוּ כּוֹרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וְנוֹפְלִים עַל פְּנֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: they would bow down on their knees and fall on their faces,
chunks.st: they would kneel and prostrate themselves and fall on their faces,

chunks.he: וְאוֹמְרִים, בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
chunks.en: and say, "Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
chunks.st: and say: Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.

summary: The goat for Azazel is given to a man who leads it out to the desert. Anyone may do it, but the Kohanim Gedolim made a rule to give it only to a Kohen.
stIntro: After the confession over the scapegoat, the priest

chunks.en: He gave it to the one who was leading it.
chunks.st: passed the goat to the one who was to lead it to the wilderness.

chunks.en: Anyone is allowed to lead it,
chunks.st: According to the halakha, everyone is eligible to lead it,

chunks.en: but the Kohanim Gedolim made it a fixed rule
chunks.st: but the High Priests established a fixed custom

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהוֹלִיכוֹ.
chunks.en: and did not let a Yisrael lead it.
chunks.explain: A Yisrael is a Jew who is not a Kohen or a Levi.
chunks.st: and did not allow an Israelite to lead it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said: That was not always the case.

chunks.en: once Arsela led it,
chunks.st: There was an incident where a person named Arsela led the goat to the wilderness,

chunks.en: and he was a Yisrael.
chunks.st: and he was an Israelite.

summary: Some people from Bavel pulled the goat's hair and told it to take away the sins. Important people walked with the man, and there were ten huts along the way to the cliff.

chunks.en: And they made a ramp for him because of the Babylonians,
chunks.st: And they made a ramp for the goat due to the Babylonian Jews who were in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: who would pull at its hair,
chunks.st: who would pluck at the goat’s hair

chunks.en: and say to it,
chunks.st: and would say to the goat:

chunks.en: "Take and go out,
chunks.explain: Take our sins away with you.
chunks.st: Take our sins and go,

chunks.en: take and go out!"
chunks.st: take our sins and go, and do not leave them with us.

chunks.en: Important people of Yerushalayim would walk with him
chunks.st: People from among the prominent residents of Jerusalem would escort the one leading the goat

chunks.en: until the first hut.
chunks.st: until they reached the first booth.
chunks.stMore: Booths were set up along the path to the wilderness to provide the escort a place to rest.

chunks.en: Ten huts from Yerushalayim to the cliff,
chunks.st: There were ten booths from Jerusalem to the cliff,

chunks.en: ninety ris,
chunks.st: with a distance of ninety ris between them.

words.note: A ris is a measure of distance.

chunks.en: seven and a half for each mil.
chunks.st: As there are seven and a half ris for each mil, the total distance was twelve mil.

words.note: A mil is about one kilometer.

summary: At each hut the people offer the man food and water. They walk with him from hut to hut, and the last one watches from far away.

chunks.he: עַל כָּל סֻכָּה וְסֻכָּה אוֹמְרִים לוֹ,
chunks.en: At each and every hut they say to him,
chunks.st: At each and every booth, people there say to him:

chunks.en: "Here is food and here is water."
chunks.explain: Just knowing he could eat made it easier for him to fast.
chunks.st: Here is food; here is water, if you need it.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains why they offered him food.

chunks.en: And they walk with him from hut to hut,
chunks.st: And they escort him from booth to booth,

chunks.en: except for the last one of them,
chunks.st: except for the last person at the last booth,

chunks.en: who does not go with him to the cliff,
chunks.st: who does not reach the cliff with him.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא עוֹמֵד מֵרָחוֹק וְרוֹאֶה אֶת מַעֲשָׂיו:
chunks.en: but stands far away and watches what he does.
chunks.st: Rather, he stands from a distance and observes his actions to ensure that he fulfills the mitzva properly.

summary: The man ties half of the red strip to a rock and half between the goat's horns, and pushes the goat off the cliff. Then he waits in the last hut until dark.

chunks.en: What would he do?
chunks.st: What did the one designated to dispatch the goat do there?

chunks.en: He divides the strip of red wool,
chunks.st: He divided a strip of crimson into two parts,

chunks.en: half he tied to the rock,
chunks.st: half of the strip tied to the rock,

chunks.en: and half he tied between its two horns,
chunks.st: and half of it tied between the two horns of the goat.

chunks.en: and pushed it backward,
chunks.st: And he pushed the goat backward,

chunks.en: and it rolls and goes down,
chunks.st: and it rolls and descends.

chunks.en: and it would not reach halfway down the mountain
chunks.st: And it would not reach halfway down the mountain

chunks.en: before it was broken into pieces.
chunks.st: until it was torn limb from limb.

chunks.he: בָּא וְיָשַׁב לוֹ תַּחַת סֻכָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה
chunks.en: He came and sat under the last hut
chunks.st: The one designated to dispatch the goat came and sat under the roofing of last booth

chunks.en: until it got dark.
chunks.st: until it grows dark and only then went home.

chunks.en: And from when do his clothes become tamei?
chunks.st: And from what point are the garments of the man rendered impure, as it is stated that he is impure and his clothes requires immersion?

chunks.en: From when he goes out of the wall of Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: From the moment he emerges outside the wall of Jerusalem.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: His clothes are rendered impure only

chunks.en: from the time he pushes it off the cliff.
chunks.st: from the moment that he pushes the goat from the cliff.

summary: The Kohen Gadol takes the special parts of the bull and goat that are burned, and burns them on the mizbeach. The rest is carried out to be burned outside Yerushalayim.
stIntro: After the High Priest passed the goat to the man tasked with dispatching the goat,

chunks.he: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל פָּר וְשָׂעִיר הַנִּשְׂרָפִין.
chunks.en: He comes to the bull and goat that are burned.
chunks.st: he came next to the bull and the goat that were to be burned.

chunks.en: He tore them open and took out their parts for the mizbeach,
chunks.st: He tore their flesh but was not required to cut it into pieces, and removed the portions of the offering consumed on the altar

chunks.en: he put them in a big bowl,
chunks.st: and placed them in a large bowl [magis]

chunks.en: and burned them on top of the mizbeach.
chunks.st: and burned them on the altar.

chunks.en: He wove them onto poles,
chunks.st: He interwove and bound the bull and the goat together into braids as one mass.
chunks.stMore: They were placed in that way upon two poles and carried by four people who

chunks.en: and took them out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: took them out to the place designated for burning, outside of Jerusalem.

chunks.en: And from when do they make clothes tamei?
chunks.explain: The people who burn them become tamei.
chunks.st: And at what point do the bull and goat render the garments of those who carried them impure,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “And he who burns them shall wash his garments” (Leviticus 16:28)?

chunks.en: From when they go out of the wall of the azarah.
chunks.st: They render the garments impure from the moment that they emerged outside the wall of the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: from when the fire catches most of them.
chunks.st: They render the garments impure from the moment that the fire has ignited in most of the bull and the goat.

summary: People waved scarves so that the Kohen Gadol would know the goat reached the desert. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yishmael say there were other signs too, like the red strip turning white.

chunks.en: They said to the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: They said to the High Priest:

chunks.en: "The goat has reached the desert."
chunks.st: The goat has reached the wilderness.

chunks.he: וּמִנַּיִן הָיוּ יוֹדְעִין שֶׁהִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר,
chunks.en: And how did they know that the goat reached the desert?
chunks.st: And how did they know in the Temple that the goat reached the wilderness?

chunks.en: They would make lookout posts,
chunks.st: They would build platforms [dirkaot] all along the way and people would stand on them

chunks.en: and wave scarves,
chunks.st: and wave scarves [sudarin] to signal when the goat arrived.

chunks.en: and they know that the goat reached the desert.
chunks.st: And therefore they knew that the goat reached the wilderness.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said: Why did they need these platforms?

chunks.en: "But didn't they have a great sign?
chunks.st: Didn’t they already have a reliable indicator?

chunks.he: מִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְעַד בֵּית חִדּוּדוֹ שְׁלשָׁה מִילִין.
chunks.en: From Yerushalayim to Beis Chidudo is three mil.
chunks.st: From Jerusalem to Beit Ḥiddudo, the edge of the wilderness, where the mitzva of dispatching the goat was performed, was a distance of three mil.

words.note: The place at the edge of the desert where the cliff was.

chunks.en: They walk a mil,
chunks.st: Since the nobles of Jerusalem walked a mil to escort the dispatcher

chunks.en: and come back a mil,
chunks.st: and returned a mil,

chunks.en: and wait the time of a mil,
chunks.st: and waited the time equivalent to the time it takes to walk a mil,

chunks.en: and they know that the goat reached the desert."
chunks.st: they knew that the goat reached the wilderness.
chunks.stMore: There was no need for the platforms.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: "But didn't they have another sign?
chunks.st: Didn’t they have a different indicator?

chunks.en: A strip of red wool was tied
chunks.st: There was a strip of crimson tied

chunks.en: on the doorway of the Heichal,
chunks.st: to the entrance to the Sanctuary,

chunks.he: וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר הָיָה הַלָּשׁוֹן מַלְבִּין,
chunks.en: and when the goat reached the desert, the strip would turn white,
chunks.explain: This showed that Hashem forgave the sins of the Jewish people.
chunks.st: and when the goat reached the wilderness and the mitzva was fulfilled the strip would turn white,

chunks.en: as it says (Yeshayahu 1),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ:
chunks.en: 'If your sins are like red, they will become white like snow.'"
chunks.st: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they will become white as snow” (Isaiah 1:18).
